payload.prompt: EXECUTION-PLAN-COMPILER: The execution-plan compiler turns a validated feature plan into an inspectable executable proposal.

payload.question: Should FEAT-018 be a hard gate in front of FEAT-013's dispatch-task, or a read-only/advisory proposal generator not yet wired as a required precondition?
payload.text: Hard gate: FEAT-018's validated proposal must be required and checked deterministically whenever the execution tool suite (dispatch-task and the rest of coherence.execution.cli) is invoked -- a task cannot be dispatched without a passing, current proposal.

payload.response: Agreed: no implementation evidence exists yet because this is the planning stage for that implementation. The hard-gate decision stands as stated in a2; evidence will exist once FEAT-018 is built.

payload.question: Should the FEAT-018 proposal be scoped per planning run/plan (one proposal covers every task generated from that plan) or per individual task?
payload.text: Per planning run/plan. Every generated task already carries source_plan in its frontmatter, so the gate can resolve a task's plan-level proposal by that reference. The proposal must be hash-bound to the plan file plus the complete generated task set (not just a boolean per run_id), and any drift in the plan or its task set after the proposal was validated invalidates the whole plan's proposal -- every remaining dispatch-task call blocks (fail-closed) until a fresh proposal is generated, not just the changed task.

payload.question: Should this FEAT-018 planning run scope down to what's actually implementable now -- the deterministic whole-plan/graph validator wired as a hard gate in front of the one canonical workflow FEAT-013 already implements -- and defer the full execution-profile catalog (direct/Kanban/interactive/headless/etc.) to a later increment?
payload.text: Yes. Scope this run to the deterministic whole-plan/graph validator and hard-gate wiring against the single existing canonical workflow/GatePlan shape FEAT-013 already implements. The multi-profile catalog (direct-single-agent, Hermes-Kanban-durable, interactive-controller, headless-CI, etc.) described in the original FEAT-018 dossier is out of scope for this run and deferred to a later increment, matching how FEAT-017 scoped down to only implemented backend capability.

payload.question: Should proposal compilation be a new required FEAT-017 planning checkpoint, a standalone execution-side command, or both?
payload.text: Both, as gates at each layer: a new required FEAT-017 planning-lifecycle checkpoint after task decomposition and before handoff, AND the execution-side hard gate at dispatch time (per a2). Concern about added load was raised but is not a blocker: the check is deterministic (file reads, hashing, structural validation, no LLM/network calls) and comparable in cost to existing gates already run routinely (compile_gate_plan, ExecutionContract.build, FEAT-017's own run-planning-gates). Per a2's 'whenever the execution tool suite is invoked,' the execution-side gate re-validates on every entry point, not only first dispatch -- including a resolve-human retry -- for the same reason.

payload.question: Correction to a9: which commands are actually gated, and does whole-plan drift block already-dispatched tasks' retries?
payload.text: Narrower than a9: only dispatch-task (starting a task) and resolve-human --decision retry (resuming an already-open task) are gated at all. legal-actions and stream-progress are read-only (gating is meaningless). report-worker-result and resolve-human --decision defer/block start no new work; gating report-worker-result would be actively harmful, stranding a worker's already-completed result under a contract that was valid when the work was done. Within dispatch-task/retry: option B applies -- once a task's ExecutionContract is compiled at first dispatch, it is immutable and that task's retries continue under it regardless of unrelated later plan/task-file changes. Whole-plan drift (a5) only blocks a fresh dispatch-task on a task that has not yet been dispatched; it does not freeze an already-dispatched task's in-flight retry loop.
